statement: Two simple graphs whose adjacency matrices have the same multiset of eigenvalues (cospectral graphs) are isomorphic.
definitions: Adjacency matrix of a simple graph on n vertices is the symmetric 0/1 n x n matrix; the spectrum is its multiset of n real eigenvalues (with multiplicity). Graphs compared must have the same number of vertices.
ground_truth_witness: G1 = K_{1,4}, the star on vertices 0..4 with edges {0,1},{0,2},{0,3},{0,4}; G2 = C4 + K1, a 4-cycle on 0,1,2,3 with edges {0,1},{1,2},{2,3},{3,0} plus an isolated vertex 4. Both have characteristic polynomial x^5 - 4x^3 (spectrum {2, 0, 0, 0, -2}), but G1 has a vertex of degree 4 while G2 has maximum degree 2, so they are not isomorphic. This is the smallest cospectral non-isomorphic pair. Edge list of G1: [[0,1],[0,2],[0,3],[0,4]]; edge list of G2: [[0,1],[0,3],[1,2],[2,3]] together with the isolated vertex 4.
reference_authority: online-cited counterexample (MO/MSE/CS.SE/Wikipedia) with verify script, verified per partB_feasibility records

skeptic.objection: Precise and false. Verified: K_{1,4} and C4+K1 both have characteristic polynomial x^5 - 4x^3 and are non-isomorphic (max degree 4 vs 2); no cospectral non-isomorphic pair exists on <=4 vertices, so this is the smallest. The roster has no 'cospectral implies isomorphic' claim and its cospectral objects (Shrikhande/rook) appear under different claims, so not a duplicate. Solver must exhibit a pair and compute spectra, so it is more than recall, but the pair is the canonical textbook example. Should NOT be admitted together with cb-mse-r14 (rejected above) since one answers both.

bank_overlap.rationale: No cospectral / characteristic-polynomial-of-a-graph / adjacency-spectrum entry exists (adjacency-matrix entries se-math-994847-q and arxiv-0709-2689v3 concern walk counts and nilpotency, not spectra). K_{1,4} alone appears as a witness in se-math-3525408-q for a path-decomposition step, but the task's object is the cospectral pair (K_{1,4}, C4+K1), which is absent.
